items.targetSentence: Revisen la barrera antes de cubrir.
items.englishTranslation: Check the house wrap before covering.
items.explanation: After 'antes de', Spanish uses the infinitive (cubrir), not a conjugated verb.

items.targetSentence: ¿Dónde va el canal J?
items.englishTranslation: Where does the J-channel go?
items.explanation: In questions, the verb (va) comes right after the question word and before the subject.

items.targetSentence: Pónganse el respirador para cortar fibrocemento.
items.englishTranslation: Put on the respirator to cut fiber cement.
items.explanation: In an affirmative command, the pronoun is attached to the end of the verb: pónganse.

items.targetSentence: Instalen la tira de arranque.
items.englishTranslation: Install the starter strip.
items.explanation: 'Tira de arranque' is noun + de + noun, so the main noun (tira) comes first.

items.targetSentence: Falta un esquinero en la troca.
items.englishTranslation: One corner post is missing from the truck.
items.explanation: 'Faltar' usually comes before its subject: Falta un esquinero.

items.targetSentence: No suban con viento fuerte.
items.englishTranslation: Don't go up in strong wind.
items.explanation: For a negative ustedes command, put 'no' before the verb; the adjective (fuerte) goes after the noun.

items.targetSentence: Señora, mañana instalamos el sofito.
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, tomorrow we install the soffit.
items.explanation: Spanish often uses the present tense for planned future actions: mañana instalamos.

items.targetSentence: Calafateen la moldura de la ventana.
items.englishTranslation: Caulk the window trim board.
items.explanation: 'The window trim' becomes 'la moldura de la ventana': the main noun comes first, then de + owner.

items.targetSentence: Pon tapajuntas arriba de la puerta.
items.englishTranslation: Put flashing above the door.
items.explanation: 'Pon' is the irregular tú command of poner, the form a coworker uses.

items.targetSentence: Recojan los clavos del pasto.
items.englishTranslation: Pick up the nails from the grass.
items.explanation: De + el always contracts to 'del': del pasto. In the command, recoger changes g to j: recojan.

items.targetSentence: Amarren el arnés al andamio.
items.englishTranslation: Tie off the harness to the scaffold.
items.explanation: Ustedes command 'Amarren' comes first; 'al' is a + el combined before a masculine noun.

items.targetSentence: ¿Está a plomo el esquinero?
items.englishTranslation: Is the corner post plumb?
items.explanation: In Spanish questions the verb often comes first and the subject 'el esquinero' goes at the end.

items.targetSentence: Corta el canal J con tijeras.
items.englishTranslation: Cut the J-channel with snips.
items.explanation: A coworker uses the tú command 'Corta'; the letter J follows 'canal', like an adjective after the noun.

items.targetSentence: Hay madera podrida en la fascia.
items.englishTranslation: There is rotten wood on the fascia.
items.explanation: 'Hay' means there is/are; the adjective 'podrida' goes after the noun 'madera' and agrees with it.

items.targetSentence: No claven el vinilo apretado.
items.englishTranslation: Don't nail the vinyl tight.
items.explanation: 'No' goes right before the command 'claven'; 'apretado' follows the noun it describes.

items.targetSentence: Señor, ¿firma aquí, por favor?
items.englishTranslation: Sir, will you sign here, please?
items.explanation: With one customer use the usted form 'firma'; the question mark ¿ opens after the name, not before it.

items.targetSentence: ¿Cuántas cajas de sofito faltan?
items.englishTranslation: How many boxes of soffit are missing?
items.explanation: 'Cuántas' agrees with 'cajas', and the verb 'faltan' goes at the end and is plural to match.

items.targetSentence: Guarden el fibrocemento bajo la lona.
items.englishTranslation: Store the fiber cement under the tarp.
items.explanation: The ustedes command 'Guarden' opens the sentence; 'bajo' (under) comes before 'la lona'.

items.targetSentence: Apaga la sierra antes de ajustarla.
items.englishTranslation: Turn off the saw before adjusting it.
items.explanation: After 'antes de' use the infinitive, and the pronoun 'la' attaches to its end: ajustarla.

items.targetSentence: La barrera necesita más traslape.
items.englishTranslation: The house wrap needs more lap.
items.explanation: The subject 'La barrera' goes before the verb, and 'más' comes right before the noun 'traslape'.

items.targetSentence: Aléjense de los cables eléctricos.
items.englishTranslation: Stay away from the power lines.
items.explanation: With an ustedes command, the reflexive pronoun attaches to the end of the verb: aléjense. The adjective eléctricos comes after cables.

items.targetSentence: Quiten el revestimiento viejo primero.
items.englishTranslation: Remove the old siding first.
items.explanation: The adjective viejo goes after revestimiento, and primero goes at the end of the command.

items.targetSentence: Marquen la línea de tiza.
items.englishTranslation: Mark the chalk line.
items.explanation: An ustedes command starts the sentence. In "línea de tiza", the main noun línea comes first and "de tiza" follows it.

items.targetSentence: El sofito ventilado va aquí.
items.englishTranslation: The vented soffit goes here.
items.explanation: The adjective ventilado follows sofito. Then come the verb va and the place word aquí.

items.targetSentence: Señor, el inspector viene mañana.
items.englishTranslation: Sir, the inspector is coming tomorrow.
items.explanation: The name or title you call someone by comes first, followed by a comma. Spanish uses the present tense viene for a planned event tomorrow.

items.targetSentence: No hay clavos en la troca.
items.englishTranslation: There are no nails in the truck.
items.explanation: No goes right before hay, and hay is used for both singular and plural nouns.

items.targetSentence: Usa lentes de seguridad, Beto.
items.englishTranslation: Wear safety glasses, Beto.
items.explanation: Usa is a tú command for a coworker. The person's name can go at the end, after a comma.

items.targetSentence: ¿Está derecha la moldura?
items.englishTranslation: Is the trim board straight?
items.explanation: In yes/no questions with estar, the verb and adjective often come before the subject. Derecha is feminine to match moldura.

items.targetSentence: Cambien el tapajuntas doblado.
items.englishTranslation: Replace the bent flashing.
items.explanation: Tapajuntas ends in -s but is singular and masculine (el tapajuntas). The adjective doblado comes after it.

items.targetSentence: Hay una rasgadura en la barrera.
items.englishTranslation: There is a tear in the house wrap.
items.explanation: Hay (there is) starts the sentence, and the place phrase "en la barrera" comes at the end.

items.targetSentence: Midan la pared norte primero.
items.englishTranslation: Measure the north wall first.
items.explanation: Midan is the ustedes command of medir (e→i), and the direction norte comes after pared.

items.targetSentence: ¿Quién tiene la pistola de calafatear?
items.englishTranslation: Who has the caulking gun?
items.explanation: The question word ¿Quién starts the sentence, and the tool's purpose follows with de + infinitive: pistola de calafatear.

items.targetSentence: Retoca los cortes del fibrocemento.
items.englishTranslation: Touch up the fiber cement cuts.
items.explanation: Retoca is a tú command to one coworker, and de + el contracts to del before fibrocemento.

items.targetSentence: Tapen las plantas con plástico.
items.englishTranslation: Cover the plants with plastic sheeting.
items.explanation: The ustedes command Tapen comes first, then the object, then con + material.

items.targetSentence: Señora, ¿le gusta este color?
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, do you like this color?
items.explanation: With gustar the thing liked (este color) is the subject, and the pronoun le goes before the verb.

items.targetSentence: La primera hilera está torcida.
items.englishTranslation: The first course is crooked.
items.explanation: Primera goes before the noun, and estar is used for a condition: está torcida.

items.targetSentence: Bajen del andamio ahora, hay rayos.
items.englishTranslation: Get down from the scaffold now, there's lightning.
items.explanation: Bajen de means get down from, so de + el becomes del, and hay gives the reason after the comma.

items.targetSentence: Necesito el número de pedido.
items.englishTranslation: I need the order number.
items.explanation: Spanish says número de pedido (number of order), so the main noun comes first, unlike English order number.

items.targetSentence: Usen sofito sólido en el porche.
items.englishTranslation: Use solid soffit on the porch.
items.explanation: The adjective sólido goes after the noun sofito, and no article is needed for the material.

items.targetSentence: Inspector, la barrera está lista.
items.englishTranslation: Inspector, the house wrap is ready.
items.explanation: Estar + lista means ready, and lista ends in -a to agree with the feminine noun barrera.

items.targetSentence: Ayer revisamos el sofito ventilado del lado sur.
items.englishTranslation: Yesterday we checked the vented soffit on the south side.
items.explanation: Preterite 'revisamos' for a finished action; the adjective 'ventilado' follows the noun 'sofito'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Puedes cortar el canal J con las tijeras?
items.englishTranslation: Can you cut the J-channel with the snips?
items.explanation: 'Poder' is conjugated and the next verb stays in the infinitive: puedes cortar.

items.targetSentence: Mañana vamos a instalar la fascia en el alero.
items.englishTranslation: Tomorrow we are going to install the fascia on the eave.
items.explanation: Ir a + infinitive expresses the plan: vamos a instalar, with the time word first.

items.targetSentence: Pongan el esquinero a plomo y luego clávenlo.
items.englishTranslation: Set the corner post plumb and then nail it.
items.explanation: In an affirmative ustedes command the pronoun attaches to the end: clávenlo, with an added accent.

items.targetSentence: Las molduras blancas van alrededor de cada ventana.
items.englishTranslation: The white trim boards go around each window.
items.explanation: The adjective follows the noun and agrees in gender and number: molduras blancas.

items.targetSentence: No dejen los paneles de vinilo al sol.
items.englishTranslation: Don't leave the vinyl panels in the sun.
items.explanation: Negative ustedes command: 'No' goes right before 'dejen'; 'de vinilo' describes the panels.

items.targetSentence: Señora, le muestro el revestimiento nuevo esta tarde.
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, I'll show you the new siding this afternoon.
items.explanation: The indirect object pronoun 'le' (to you, formal) comes before the conjugated verb 'muestro'.

items.targetSentence: Encontré el tapajuntas roto arriba de la ventana.
items.englishTranslation: I found the broken flashing above the window.
items.explanation: Preterite 'encontré' reports the finding; 'roto' follows 'tapajuntas', which is masculine.

items.targetSentence: Amarren la escalera arriba antes de subir.
items.englishTranslation: Tie off the ladder at the top before climbing.
items.explanation: After 'antes de' Spanish uses the infinitive: antes de subir.

items.targetSentence: ¿Ya pegaron cinta en las costuras de la barrera?
items.englishTranslation: Did you already put tape on the house wrap seams?
items.explanation: 'Ya' opens the question, and the preterite 'pegaron' goes with ustedes.

items.targetSentence: Mañana tenemos que cambiar la moldura podrida.
items.englishTranslation: Tomorrow we have to replace the rotten trim board.
items.explanation: Tener que comes before the infinitive, and the adjective podrida goes after the noun and agrees with feminine moldura.

items.targetSentence: ¿Dónde guardaste las tijeras para lámina?
items.englishTranslation: Where did you put away the tin snips?
items.explanation: The preterite tú form guardaste comes right after the question word, and para lámina follows tijeras.

items.targetSentence: Antes de cortar fibrocemento, pónganse el respirador.
items.englishTranslation: Before cutting fiber cement, put on your respirators.
items.explanation: Antes de takes an infinitive, and the pronoun se attaches to the end of the affirmative ustedes command pónganse.

items.targetSentence: Ayer el inspector firmó la tarjeta del andamio.
items.englishTranslation: Yesterday the inspector signed the scaffold tag.
items.explanation: Firmó is preterite for a finished action, and del (de + el) links tarjeta to andamio.

items.targetSentence: Disculpe, ¿puede mover su carro de la entrada?
items.englishTranslation: Excuse me, can you move your car out of the driveway?
items.explanation: Use usted with a customer: puede is followed directly by the infinitive mover.

items.targetSentence: La tira de arranque no está a nivel.
items.englishTranslation: The starter strip is not level.
items.explanation: No goes right before the verb, and estar is used because being level is a condition.

items.targetSentence: Vamos a calafatear las juntas mañana temprano.
items.englishTranslation: We are going to caulk the seams early tomorrow.
items.explanation: Ir a + infinitive talks about the future, and the time words mañana temprano usually go at the end.

items.targetSentence: Falta una caja de esquineros en el pedido.
items.englishTranslation: One box of corner posts is missing from the order.
items.explanation: Faltar usually comes before its subject, and it is singular here because the subject is una caja.

items.targetSentence: Clávenlo en el centro de la ranura, por favor.
items.englishTranslation: Nail it in the center of the slot, please.
items.explanation: The object pronoun lo attaches to the end of an affirmative command, so clavar becomes clávenlo with an accent.

items.targetSentence: No pongan la escalera cerca de los cables eléctricos.
items.englishTranslation: Don't put the ladder near the power lines.
items.explanation: A negative ustedes command is just no + pongan, and the adjective eléctricos goes after cables and agrees with it.

items.targetSentence: El tapajuntas va debajo de la barrera, no encima.
items.englishTranslation: The flashing goes under the house wrap, not on top.
items.explanation: "Debajo de" needs "de" before the noun, but "encima" stands alone at the end because nothing follows it.

items.targetSentence: Juan, ¿ya mediste el hueco de la ventila?
items.englishTranslation: Juan, did you already measure the opening for the vent?
items.explanation: The question mark ¿ opens after the name, and "ya" comes before the preterite verb "mediste".

items.targetSentence: El proveedor entregó los esquineros equivocados esta mañana.
items.englishTranslation: The supplier delivered the wrong corner posts this morning.
items.explanation: The adjective "equivocados" follows the noun and is masculine plural to match "esquineros".

items.targetSentence: Ese panel de fibrocemento está rajado; no lo instalen.
items.englishTranslation: That fiber cement panel is cracked; don't install it.
items.explanation: In a negative command, the pronoun "lo" goes before the verb: "no lo instalen".

items.targetSentence: Voy a llamar al proveedor por el canal F.
items.englishTranslation: I'm going to call the supplier about the F-channel.
items.explanation: Ir a + infinitive gives the future plan, and a + el contracts to "al" before "proveedor".

items.targetSentence: Señor, mañana tenemos que quitar su luz exterior.
items.englishTranslation: Sir, tomorrow we have to remove your outdoor light.
items.explanation: "Tener que" + infinitive means "have to", and the adjective "exterior" comes after "luz".

items.targetSentence: Bajen del andamio ahora; viene una tormenta eléctrica.
items.englishTranslation: Get down from the scaffold now; a lightning storm is coming.
items.explanation: The ustedes command "Bajen" goes first, and in the second clause the verb "viene" comes before its subject.

items.targetSentence: ¿Me puedes pasar la pistola de calafatear?
items.englishTranslation: Can you pass me the caulking gun?
items.explanation: The pronoun "me" can go before "puedes" instead of being attached to "pasar".

items.targetSentence: Inspector, ¿puede revisar la barrera antes de cubrirla?
items.englishTranslation: Inspector, can you check the house wrap before we cover it?
items.explanation: After "antes de" the verb stays an infinitive, and the pronoun "la" attaches to its end: "cubrirla".

items.targetSentence: Hay dos rayones en la fascia blanca; retóquenlos hoy.
items.englishTranslation: There are two scratches on the white fascia; touch them up today.
items.explanation: In a positive command, "los" attaches to the end of the verb, and the accent keeps the stress: "retóquenlos".

items.targetSentence: Ayer cambiamos el canal J de la puerta trasera.
items.englishTranslation: Yesterday we replaced the J-channel at the back door.
items.explanation: The preterite 'cambiamos' tells about yesterday, and the adjective 'trasera' comes after 'puerta'.

items.targetSentence: No lo claven apretado; el vinilo necesita moverse.
items.englishTranslation: Don't nail it tight; the vinyl needs to move.
items.explanation: In a negative command, the pronoun 'lo' goes before the verb: 'No lo claven'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Quién guardó la tira de arranque en la troca?
items.englishTranslation: Who put the starter strip away in the truck?
items.explanation: The question starts with '¿Quién' and the preterite verb 'guardó' comes right after it.

items.targetSentence: Señora, vamos a tapar sus ventanas con plástico.
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, we are going to cover your windows with plastic sheeting.
items.explanation: 'Ir a' plus an infinitive shows a plan: 'vamos a tapar'. The word 'sus' goes before the noun.

items.targetSentence: Tienes que ponerte los protectores de oídos, Beto.
items.englishTranslation: You have to put on your ear protection, Beto.
items.explanation: After 'tener que', the reflexive pronoun attaches to the infinitive: 'ponerte'.

items.targetSentence: El sofito de vinilo entra en el canal F.
items.englishTranslation: The vinyl soffit goes into the F-channel.
items.explanation: 'De vinilo' comes after the noun to describe it, and the letter F goes after 'canal'.

items.targetSentence: Midan dos veces la moldura antes de cortarla.
items.englishTranslation: Measure the trim board twice before cutting it.
items.explanation: After 'antes de', the pronoun 'la' attaches to the end of the infinitive: 'cortarla'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Le avisaste al contratista de la madera podrida?
items.englishTranslation: Did you let the contractor know about the rotten wood?
items.explanation: 'Le' goes before the verb even though 'al contratista' also names the person, and 'podrida' comes after 'madera'.

items.targetSentence: Apaguen la sierra antes de cambiar el disco.
items.englishTranslation: Turn off the saw before changing the blade.
items.explanation: The ustedes command 'Apaguen' comes first, and 'antes de' is followed by an infinitive.

items.targetSentence: Hoy no podemos subir; el andamio no tiene barandal.
items.englishTranslation: Today we can't go up; the scaffold has no guardrail.
items.explanation: 'No' goes right before the conjugated verb 'podemos', and the infinitive 'subir' follows it.

items.targetSentence: Antes de que instalen el canal J, revisen el tapajuntas de la ventana.
items.englishTranslation: Before you install the J-channel, check the window flashing.
items.explanation: 'Antes de que' always takes the subjunctive: instalen, not instalan.

items.targetSentence: Señora, ¿podría mover su carro para que bajemos el material?
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, could you move your car so we can unload the material?
items.explanation: The conditional 'podría' makes the request polite, and 'para que' takes the subjunctive 'bajemos'.

items.targetSentence: Es importante que dejen espacio en los extremos del vinilo por el calor.
items.englishTranslation: It's important that you leave a gap at the ends of the vinyl because of the heat.
items.explanation: 'Es importante que' triggers the subjunctive: dejen, not dejan.

items.targetSentence: Si el esquinero no está a plomo, no sigan con los paneles.
items.englishTranslation: If the corner post isn't plumb, don't continue with the panels.
items.explanation: After 'si' use the indicative (está); the negative command for ustedes is 'no sigan'.

items.targetSentence: Nadie sube al andamio hasta que el jefe de cuadrilla revise los barandales.
items.englishTranslation: Nobody goes up on the scaffold until the crew lead checks the guardrails.
items.explanation: 'Hasta que' about a future event takes the subjunctive: revise, not revisa.

items.targetSentence: Pongan el sofito ventilado en el alero para que el techo tenga ventilación.
items.englishTranslation: Put the vented soffit on the eave so the roof gets ventilation.
items.explanation: The adjective 'ventilado' follows 'sofito', and 'para que' takes the subjunctive 'tenga'.

items.targetSentence: Sería mejor cambiar esa moldura porque la madera de atrás está podrida.
items.englishTranslation: It would be better to replace that trim board because the wood behind it is rotten.
items.explanation: The conditional 'sería' softens the advice; 'porque' gives a fact, so it takes the indicative 'está'.

items.targetSentence: Avísame cuando termines la fascia, y subimos el sofito juntos.
items.englishTranslation: Let me know when you finish the fascia, and we'll take the soffit up together.
items.explanation: The pronoun attaches to the tú command (avísame), and 'cuando' about the future takes the subjunctive 'termines'.

items.targetSentence: Cuando claven el fibrocemento, no dejen la cabeza del clavo hundida.
items.englishTranslation: When you nail the fiber cement, don't leave the nail head sunk in.
items.explanation: 'Cuando' for an upcoming action takes the subjunctive 'claven'; 'hundida' follows and agrees with 'cabeza'.

items.targetSentence: Necesitamos que el proveedor entregue la tira de arranque antes del lunes.
items.englishTranslation: We need the supplier to deliver the starter strip before Monday.
items.explanation: 'Necesitamos que' plus a new subject takes the subjunctive 'entregue'; 'antes del' comes before a noun, without 'que'.

items.targetSentence: Revisen que la barrera no tenga rasgaduras antes de que llegue el inspector.
items.englishTranslation: Check that the house wrap has no tears before the inspector arrives.
items.explanation: Both 'revisen que' and 'antes de que' take the subjunctive here: tenga, llegue.

items.targetSentence: Señor, ¿le molestaría que empecemos más temprano mañana por el calor?
items.englishTranslation: Sir, would you mind if we start earlier tomorrow because of the heat?
items.explanation: The polite conditional 'le molestaría' is followed by que + subjunctive (empecemos); 'le' comes before the verb.

items.targetSentence: Aunque sea un solo corte, nadie corta fibrocemento sin la aspiradora.
items.englishTranslation: Even if it is just one cut, nobody cuts fiber cement without the vacuum.
items.explanation: 'Aunque' + subjunctive (sea) means 'even if'; the clause comes first and is followed by a comma.

items.targetSentence: Pregúntale al proveedor si el pedido de sofito ya viene en camino.
items.englishTranslation: Ask the supplier if the soffit order is already on its way.
items.explanation: The pronoun attaches to the tú command (pregúntale), and the indirect question with 'si' uses the indicative.

items.targetSentence: Instalen el canal F en la pared antes de cortar el sofito.
items.englishTranslation: Install the F-channel on the wall before cutting the soffit.
items.explanation: With the same subject, use 'antes de' + infinitive (cortar), not 'antes de que' + subjunctive.

items.targetSentence: Bajen la escalera cuando la muevan cerca de los cables eléctricos.
items.englishTranslation: Lower the ladder when you move it near the power lines.
items.explanation: 'Cuando' about a future action takes the subjunctive (muevan), and the object pronoun 'la' goes before it.

items.targetSentence: ¿Le parece bien si movemos sus plantas para que no se dañen?
items.englishTranslation: Is it all right with you if we move your plants so they don't get damaged?
items.explanation: 'Si' takes the indicative (movemos), but 'para que' requires the subjunctive (se dañen).

items.targetSentence: Tomen fotos del moho antes de que cubramos la pared.
items.englishTranslation: Take photos of the mold before we cover the wall.
items.explanation: With a different subject after it, 'antes de que' takes the subjunctive (cubramos), and de + el becomes 'del'.

items.targetSentence: Yo usaría el sellador que recomienda el fabricante en esa junta.
items.englishTranslation: I would use the caulk the manufacturer recommends on that seam.
items.explanation: The conditional 'usaría' gives soft advice; in the relative clause, the verb often comes before its subject (recomienda el fabricante).

items.targetSentence: No claven el esquinero hasta que yo revise la línea de tiza.
items.englishTranslation: Don't nail the corner post until I check the chalk line.
items.explanation: 'Hasta que' about something that hasn't happened yet takes the subjunctive (revise); 'no' goes before the command.

items.targetSentence: Quiero que calafateen las juntas de la moldura antes de que oscurezca.
items.englishTranslation: I want you to caulk the trim board joints before it gets dark.
items.explanation: Quiero que and antes de que both take the subjunctive: calafateen, oscurezca.

items.targetSentence: Si falta tira de arranque, avísenme para que yo llame al proveedor.
items.englishTranslation: If starter strip is short, let me know so I can call the supplier.
items.explanation: Si takes the indicative (falta), but para que needs the subjunctive (llame); the pronoun attaches to the command: avísenme.

items.targetSentence: Disculpe, ¿podría firmar la muestra para que hagamos el pedido?
items.englishTranslation: Excuse me, could you sign the sample so we can place the order?
items.explanation: The conditional podría makes a polite request, and para que is followed by the subjunctive hagamos.

items.targetSentence: Cuando corten el fibrocemento, pónganse el respirador aunque usen la aspiradora.
items.englishTranslation: When you cut the fiber cement, put on your respirator even if you use the vacuum.
items.explanation: Cuando about a future action takes the subjunctive (corten); the reflexive se attaches to the command pónganse.

items.targetSentence: Es necesario que se amarren con el arnés antes de subir el elevador.
items.englishTranslation: You need to tie off with the harness before raising the lift.
items.explanation: Es necesario que triggers the subjunctive amarren, with se before the verb; antes de is followed by an infinitive.

items.targetSentence: El inspector no aprueba la barrera si los traslapes quedan al revés.
items.englishTranslation: The inspector won't approve the house wrap if the laps end up reversed.
items.explanation: The si clause can come after the main clause, and it keeps the present indicative: quedan.

items.targetSentence: Le avisamos cuando terminemos el sofito para que revise el trabajo.
items.englishTranslation: We'll let you know when we finish the soffit so you can check the work.
items.explanation: Le goes before the verb; cuando about the future and para que both take the subjunctive: terminemos, revise.

items.targetSentence: Mide el hueco del medidor dos veces para que no repitamos el corte.
items.englishTranslation: Measure the opening for the meter twice so we don't have to redo the cut.
items.explanation: Mide is the tú command for a coworker; no goes right before the subjunctive repitamos after para que.

items.phraseTranslation: I don't know anyone on the crew who [verb] the J-channel better than Ana.
items.explanation: A negative antecedent ('no conozco a nadie que') takes the present subjunctive, singular for 'nadie'.

items.phrase: Si ayer ustedes ___ la pila de fibrocemento con la lona, hoy los paneles no estarían mojados.
items.phraseTranslation: If you all [verb] the fiber cement stack with the tarp yesterday, the panels wouldn't be wet today.
items.explanation: A contrary-to-fact past condition ('si ayer') takes the pluperfect subjunctive, plural for 'ustedes'.

items.phrase: Aunque el contratista nos presione, nosotros no ___ con el revestimiento hasta que el tapajuntas esté revisado.
items.phraseTranslation: Even if the contractor pressures us, we won't [verb] with the siding until the flashing is checked.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive 'presione' and 'esté' point to a real future, so the main clause takes the future, nosotros: 'seguiremos'.

items.phrase: Antes de cortar el fibrocemento, el supervisor exige que Carlos ___ la aspiradora a la sierra.
items.phraseTranslation: Before cutting the fiber cement, the supervisor demands that Carlos [verb] the vacuum to the saw.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'exige que' triggers the subjunctive, the present tense of 'exige' keeps it present, and Carlos is singular.

items.phrase: Si el cliente nos lo pidiera, nosotros ___ también las ventanas del garaje con plástico y cinta.
items.phraseTranslation: If the client asked us, we would also [verb] the garage windows with plastic and tape.
items.explanation: Conditional: 'si' + imperfect subjunctive 'pidiera' calls for the conditional, and 'nosotros' is the subject.

items.phrase: Le dije a Beto que no subiera hasta que él mismo ___ la escalera arriba.
items.phraseTranslation: I told Beto not to go up until he himself [verb] the ladder at the top.
items.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive: 'hasta que' about a pending action inside a past order ('le dije') needs the past subjunctive, singular 'él'.

items.phrase: Es importante que tú ___ cada corte del fibrocemento con una brocha pequeña, según las instrucciones del fabricante.
items.phraseTranslation: It is important that you [verb] each fiber cement cut with a small brush, according to the manufacturer's instructions.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'es importante que' triggers the subjunctive in the present, and the subject is 'tú'.

items.phrase: Cuando ustedes ___ el andamio en el lado norte la semana que viene, revisen la tarjeta de inspección.
items.phraseTranslation: When you all [verb] the scaffold on the north side next week, check the inspection tag.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'cuando' about a future action ('la semana que viene') takes the subjunctive, and 'ustedes' is plural.

items.phrase: Si Ana viera un tablón roto en el andamio, lo ___ antes de subir.
items.phraseTranslation: If Ana saw a broken plank on the scaffold, she would [verb] it before going up.
items.explanation: Conditional: a hypothetical 'si' + imperfect subjunctive ('viera') takes the conditional, and Ana is singular.

items.phrase: Dudo que los ayudantes ___ bien la lona ayer con tanto viento.
items.phraseTranslation: I doubt that the helpers [verb] the tarp well yesterday with so much wind.
items.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive: 'dudo que' triggers the subjunctive, 'ayer' makes it past, and 'los ayudantes' is plural.

items.phrase: Mañana, en cuanto el equipo ___ el revestimiento viejo de la pared norte, tomen fotos del daño.
items.phraseTranslation: Tomorrow, as soon as the crew [verb] the old siding from the north wall, take photos of the damage.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'en cuanto' about a future action ('mañana') takes the subjunctive, and 'el equipo' is singular.
